newsitem.title: CHINA: Dajiang profits down sharply on costs growth.
newsitem.headline: Dajiang profits down sharply on costs growth.

text.p: Shanghai Dajiang (Group) Co Ltd, one of China's biggest feed producers, on Monday reported a 39.49 percent fall in net profits for 1996 and a spokesman blamed rising costs.
The company's 1996 net profit was 118.72 million yuan, down from 196.19 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards, a company statement said.
According to domestic accounting standards, the company's net profits in 1996 totalled 130.8 million yuan, down 34.24 percent from the previous year's 198.9 million yuan, it said.
"Rising costs and flat sales squeezed profit margins, resulting in a sharp fall in 1996's net profits," a company official said. He declined to give further details.
Dajiang's 1996 turnover was 2,525.1 million yuan, down 1.09 percent from 2,552.9 million yuan in 1995, the company statement said.
Dajiang's B share ended Monday's trade at $0.500, unchanged from Friday's close. Its A shares put on 0.67 yuan or 6.35 percent to 11.22 yuan on Monday.
Trading in the company's shares will be suspended on Tuesday morning, the statement said.
